evidence: Figure 1 : Overview of X-World . The video backbone is first adapted on robot and human videos with one to three camera views (left). A layer-aligned Q-Former then compresses its features into fixed-length tokens that condition the action DiT, while dataset-specific projections map native states and actions to and from the shared expert (right). Action pretraining learns this interface with the video backbone frozen; target-domain post-training updates all modules using video and action supervision.
